approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds from a score-ranked population of molecules and uses a count-fingerprint Gaussian process, fitted to all accepted observations in the current session, to select purchases from newly generated graphs. Ordinary single-parent proposals come from a learned fragment-addition or directed-deletion policy. A source-and-action cache conditions that policy on known construction and admission outcomes, while retaining support for untried actions and allowing temporary pool exclusions to expire. The editor trains by maximum likelihood on purchased edits that improve their original source. The inherited crossover branch, bounded fallback, survival rule and stalled posterior-mean screen remain part of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Change which exact actions earn replay credit: a purchased editor action must beat the best real score known before its whole batch was announced. All members use that same saved reference. This should stop the learner from reinforcing edits whose success consists only of beating a weak source, and direct later learned proposals toward greater progress beyond the incumbent. The cache and training rule stay inherited. There are no completed same-Parent siblings in the brief. Earlier work changed admission efficiency or weighted parent identities; this intervention changes only exact-action replay membership. Useful stepping stones may be lost, so the decisive measurement includes every ordinary purchase and every zero-gain session.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-a8f828a5ff9b efficiently finds admissible exact fragment edits but still teaches its policy from improvements over possibly weak sources. Its admission cache remains confirmed/not_triggered: late duplicate fraction is 0.05278203212311541 versus 0.7683634442372723 in n-cd97f70a82cb, and late ordinary positive source gain increases to 0.0031658616333556685. Yet full ordinary sequential incumbent-gain mass falls from 0.13742659423856823 to 0.11494158661540828 per session, late source mean falls to 0.4808708566823216, and endpoint mean is 0.547178938842398 (SD 0.011719824443379934), an actual-Parent delta of -0.010117519877945366. A complete read-only audit of its 4350 purchases reproduces 379 source-positive policy replay labels: only 139 beat the shared pre-announcement incumbent, 136 before terminal feedback; 240 are source-only improvements. Every one of the fifteen sessions has at least two qualifying records and first exposure by batch seven. This establishes a testable replay-consumer opportunity, not that excluded edits are harmful or that the Child will see the same labels. Source evidence is nodes/n-a8f828a5ff9b/analysis.json, nodes/n-cd97f70a82cb/analysis.json, and the individually cited Parent summaries, logs and trajectories in policy/scratch/r0077-00-improve-L01/plan/support-audit.json and its audit-seed files. The formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de remains a distinct comparator at 0.607030316211131. Contrary context from nodes/n-030a6ccbba7c/analysis.json concerns smoothed parent-identity allocation: it increased progress counts but reduced total gain and endpoints. That result does not establish a capability or settle this exact-action replay-membership test.

hypothesis: Incumbent-qualified exact-action replay on the actual admission-conditioned learned-editor Parent. For announced batch b, freeze I_b=max of the scores of all real accepted observations available before that announcement. For a uniquely reconciled purchased editor action a with finite real score y, append the existing exact-action record to positive replay iff y>I_b; retain y-source_score only as a passive receipt. A policy action that improves its source but not I_b remains accepted by the GP/archive and survival consumers and receives no editor replay credit. Use the same I_b for every member, strict comparison without epsilon, and retain all previously admitted positive records even after future incumbents rise. Uniform replay sampling and the original unconditioned action log likelihood then update later source-conditioned proposals. Activation requires correct membership, actual real-label learning and changed raw probabilities on later paid actions; selecting a higher-score replay subset is not useful transfer. The useful-transfer prediction is strictly greater full ordinary-route sequential incumbent-gain mass per session than 0.11494158661540828.

finding_summary.headline: Incumbent-qualified replay learns, but ordinary incumbent progress falls
finding_summary.insights: The result rules out missing replay exposure, an arrival-order threshold, forgotten labels and an inactive learner as explanations for this intervention's failure. Improving over stronger sources still did not produce more total ordinary progress: the late source mean rose from 0.480871 to 0.503832, but ordinary purchases fell from 2,076 to 1,907 and their share fell from 47.7% to 43.8%. Only 89 of the 1,907 ordinary purchases advanced the sequential incumbent, versus 96 of 2,076 in the Parent. Sparse credit remains a concrete limitation: sessions held only 1 to 25 replay records, and three sessions had no positive addition action. These observations do not establish that excluded stepping stones caused the loss; the adaptive sources, proposed graphs and posterior-selected route mixture changed together. The route decomposition is order-dependent and cannot assign the compensating crossover gain to crossover itself. The molecular assessment supports a more specific diagnosis than global scaffold collapse: total typed scaffold coverage increased from 1,387 to 1,456, while compact aromatic-carbonyl and fused-dione high-score subsets contained only six and four generic scaffolds. Uneven access to useful connected cores and linkers persists alongside tiny fragments, repeated-core growth, unusual bonds and unresolved stereochemistry. A proposal operator or search scheme that changes cores and linkers while preserving useful molecular context could address this local-convergence limitation; these results do not establish its benefit or isolate the GP ranker as the cause. The retained MARS-inspired raw exact-action likelihood operated, as did the borrowed best-observed reference. Their combination here is a GP-selected replay adaptation, with a fixed corpus-derived fragment vocabulary; it reproduces neither MARS annealed chains nor a Jiang nonmyopic rollout, and imports no paper performance guarantee. This settles the registered replay-membership useful-transfer prediction under this panel. It preserves the Parent's confirmed admission-cache result and leaves broader learned-editor designs and retained-component contributions open.
finding_summary.results: All fifteen sessions completed, and the replay rule was implemented exactly. It admitted 127 real editor actions (54 additions and 73 deletions), excluded 206 source-only improvements, and retained every earlier admitted record. The code Parent trained on 379 source-improving actions. The Child performed 10,175 finite gradient updates and changed the raw probabilities of 1,318 later purchased actions, with learning exposure in every session. All 4,350 purchases matched accepted labels; all 4,200 nonterminal labels reached the next actual GP fit, including excluded source-only successes. Nevertheless, the registered full-session ordinary-route incumbent gain fell from 0.114942 to 0.092254, a change of -0.022688 per session; each of the three seed means declined. The downstream falsifier therefore triggered. Full and late positive source gains rose slightly, from 0.004181 to 0.004283 and from 0.003166 to 0.003398 per ordinary purchase. Final mean score was 0.546005 versus the code Parent's 0.547179: paired change -0.001174, below the separate +0.002 target. Seed macro changes were +0.026367, +0.012032 and -0.041919. The distinct formal Anchor averaged 0.607030, giving a -0.061025 comparison; trusted paired task safety passed against the code Parent and failed against the formal Anchor on sitagliptin. This is an executed intervention with a refuted useful-transfer prediction, not a technical failure or absent learning.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich indole amides, cyclic aryl amines and fused diones, with unresolved stereochemistry and unusual bonds and ring topologies
molecular.overall_character: This report describes accepted molecular output from n-db9d21d15567. The frozen comparison separately marks Child evaluation and pairing with actual code Parent n-a8f828a5ff9b complete for Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. All listed Child and published Parent trajectories were read; no task, path or paired chemistry comparison is missing. Formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de is distinct and is not the chemistry comparator. Each side contains 4350 accepted optimizer proposals; the fixed initial observations are retained in the audits but excluded from population descriptors. The assessment does not cover every internally generated, rejected or unpurchased graph. The dominant chemistry comprises indole carboxamides and alpha-ketoamides, N-rich aromatic assemblies, cyclic aryl amines, aryl sulfonamides and fused diones/iminones. The digest ring-closure rates span 0.9471 to 0.9736 and aromatic-text rates 0.9356 to 0.9713. These are molecule-level text-presence rates, not ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. RDKit parses all 4350 accepted Child structures. Median size is 29 heavy atoms, median perceived ring count is 4 and median aromatic ring count is 3; the size range is 1 to 120 heavy atoms. The code Parent has median 30 heavy atoms and the same ring medians. Chemistry quality is mixed: recognizable medicinal-chemistry frameworks coexist with 284 N-halogen, 120 O-halogen, 96 divalent O-O and 56 acyl-halide-containing structures. Parent counts under the same definitions are 542, 27, 177 and 34. These overlapping structural flags indicate liabilities to inspect, not measured stability, toxicity or synthesis failure. There are 113 structures with a perceived ring of at most four atoms all marked aromatic, versus 5 in the Parent; the leading aza-rich series contains an unusual four-member ring. There are 179 structures with at most 6 heavy atoms and 275 with at least 50, versus 171 and 413 in the Parent. Smaller size tails and fewer N-halogen bonds therefore do not imply uniformly improved chemical plausibility. No accepted Child proposal has an assigned atom stereocentre; 1572 contain an unassigned centre, compared with 1696 in the Parent, which also has no assigned centres. Only 18 Child structures carry a formal charge, versus 13 in the Parent. This describes the submitted representation, not solution protonation. The full panel has 1456 typed and 1151 generic Murcko scaffolds versus Parent 1387 and 1127, while high-score subsets remain concentrated in particular families. Diversity is moderate, with substantial ring/connectivity variation and strong local convergence. All descriptors are read-only derivations from the supplied Search molecules, not new objective scores. A high or low stratum below contains the highest or lowest 29 accepted optimizer scores per seed, combined to 87 per task; ties are ordered by evaluation. Ring counts use RDKit perception and can include symmetry-related cycles; an empty Murcko scaffold counts as one scaffold. SMARTS definitions are explicit in every audit; in particular the aliphatic-carbon carbonyl/amide flags do not count every aromatic lactam/dione, so chemical descriptions also inspect the SMILES. The trajectories do not identify a unique missing target pharmacophore, establish synthetic routes or determine the score value of unobserved stereoisomers. Shared initials, paired seeds and ancestry are dependent evidence. Chemical associations do not decide replay activation, success, selection or component contribution. Frozen digest/comparison: policy/requests/r0077-00-improve-L01-molecular-assess-3124adf8809b717b.json. Descriptor audit: policy/scratch/r0077-00-improve-L01/molecular/summary.json. Raw preservation/provenance: policy/scratch/r0077-00-improve-L01/molecular/provenance.json. The seed-0 leader is a 24-heavy-atom indole alpha-ketoamide with an N-fluoromethyl-N-phenyl amide. Seed 1 instead favors an N-brominated indole hydrazide, and seed 2 an N-chlorinated indole anilide with fluoromethoxy and N-fluoromethyl groups. Indole amide chemistry is conventionally accessible, while the N-halogen and hydrazide variants have additional stability and synthesis questions. The scores support retaining informative aromatic context; they do not establish that an unobserved saturated substitute would improve this objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: For source n-db9d21d15567 on the frozen complete accepted Search panel, 1572 of 4350 proposals have unassigned atom centres and none has an assigned centre. Their objective value must be learned from the clean current session; no stereoselectivity or ionisation benefit is established by this audit.

transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently preserve informative molecular context while controlling fragmentation and repeated-core growth.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support connected substitutions and coherent core/linker replacements that preserve several empirically useful groups together while allowing meaningful growth or contraction. The observed tails motivate generator coverage, not a universal fixed size cutoff or a claim that removing all small and large molecules has already improved search.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-db9d21d15567 has 1456 typed and 1151 generic Murcko scaffolds across the complete accepted Search panel, versus code Parent n-a8f828a5ff9b at 1387 and 1127, so global scaffold collapse would be inaccurate. Nevertheless, compact aromatic-carbonyl and fused dione high-score strata contain only 6 and 4 generic scaffolds, versus Parent 7 and 9; cyclic-amine high-score coverage increases to 37 from 30. Nitriles, sulfonamides, carbonyl-linked aromatics and saturated ring amines are all available, with uneven coverage of their chemically compatible combinations. transferable_gaps.gap: Available ring and functional-group types do not translate into consistently broad high-score combinations of core connectivity and linker chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide coherent scaffold, ring-saturation and linker changes that retain useful aromatic and polar context, with sufficient support for chemically different arrangements instead of only terminal decoration. Distinguish free amine centres from amide/sulfonamide nitrogens and conventional ethers from N,O-acetal or peroxide connections. Let each task-blind session determine which combinations matter; no benchmark-specific scaffold recipe or uniform diversification benefit is supported.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
